constraints: Source repositories are audit inputs; writes are bounded evidence artifacts, not remediation.
Configured commands and static findings never become executed verification or provider proof.
Missing, stale, and unsupported evidence remain explicit.
Projection never upgrades evidence strength or silently executes remediation.
QR-native planning and GSD planning remain independent; QR does not rewrite GSD state.
Preserve stable remediation identifiers and links to the originating audit.
Checkpoint components must match audit time, target identity, and hashes; publication coherence does not imply quality readiness.
Legacy behavior contracts remain compatible without pretending edge evidence exists.
Tier 1 and Tier 2 observations never widen Tier-0 release readiness; no self-issued independent edge verification.
Preserve baseline lineage; configuration or tool identity drift requires explicit reconciliation.
New enforced findings, unknown delta evidence, and failed required certified gates block eligibility.
Fast or cached observations cannot substitute for exact-current authoritative release evidence.
Preserve canonical root intent and prior decision history.
Metadata and environment checks do not establish application acceptance or deployment readiness.
bindings.handoff_review: Maintenance preserves the ratified map and environment. Declared subsystems own evidence and consumer handoffs; metadata grants no mutation, publication or release authority.
